description: Hold npm updates for the same 7 days as Yarn's npmMinimalAgeGate (1w), so Renovate never proposes a version Yarn will quarantine.

The top-level minimumReleaseAge does not achieve this on its own: config:best-practices extends security:minimumReleaseAgeNpm, which sets minimumReleaseAge to 3 days via a packageRule on matchDatasources npm, and a matching packageRule overrides top-level config. Without this rule the effective npm gate is 3 days.

matchUpdateTypes is load-bearing, not decoration. The same preset sets minimumReleaseAge to null for npm pin, replacement, bump, lockfileUpdate, rollback and lockFileMaintenance updates, because those types carry no releaseTimestamp. A rule matching the datasource alone would come after those carve-outs and clobber them back to an age gate they cannot satisfy, leaving their PRs permanently pending. Listing only the version-bump types leaves the carve-outs intact.
Do not let a missing releaseTimestamp block an update whose type never has one.

minimumReleaseAgeBehaviour defaults to timestamp-required, so with any minimumReleaseAge set the branch-stage stability check reads a missing upgrade.releaseTimestamp as 'has not met minimum release age' and stays pending forever rather than ageing out (renovatebot/renovate#45236). config:best-practices pins digests via docker:pinDigests and helpers:pinGitHubActionDigests, so digest updates are a permanent class here, and an open GitHub Action digest PR was pending on exactly this.

The update types listed mirror Renovate's own unsupported-type list in security.preset.ts, plus digest and pinDigest. For npm the preset already nulls most of them; this covers every other datasource, where no such carve-out exists.
